status_reason: Fig. 1's design, geometry, timing and measure are the paper's, but on a modern frame-based display (motion steps rounded to whole frames, uncalibrated white instead of the paper's 15 cd/m2 P4-phosphor CRT) and with 20 unstated details assumed, including how noise dots choose directions, the test levels and the control display.

original.citation: Hiris, E., & Blake, R. (1992). Another perspective on the visual motion aftereffect. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA, 89(19), 9025-9028.
original.experiments: Fig. 1: forced-choice matching of the dynamic motion aftereffect with real motion (adapted and no-adaptation curves); not the Fig. 2-3 discrimination experiments or the Fig. 4 bandwidth/duration experiment

notes: Two parameter sets, run as separate sessions: adapted to upward motion (configs/task.yaml) and no adaptation (configs/task-control.yaml). Set the display to the paper's white (15 cd/m2) with a photometer. No participant data: tests and simulated sessions verify the software only.
